commits.message:
test(seam): copy only regular files into the tarball stage (rich-artifact-c9k.3)

A nested repository or a submodule is listed by git ls-files as a
directory, and copyFileSync threw on it before the build ever ran. A
fresh checkout would not carry its contents either, so the stage now
takes only regular files.

test(seam): build and pack the tarball to gate its contents (rich-artifact-c9k.3)

The artifact fixes from c9k.1 and c9k.2 are each one line in a different
file (a root LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES in `files`, sourceMap and
declarationMap off, a clean step in `build`), and nothing read the tarball
back. test/seam/tarball.test.ts copies the checkout into a temp directory,
runs the real `npm run build`, and asks `npm pack --dry-run --json` what
would ship. It fails when LICENSE or THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES is missing or
empty, when a .map entry ships, or when a packed file carries a
sourceMappingURL. That last case covers excluding *.map from `files`,
which c9k.2 rejected for leaving the same dead reference.

It builds rather than reading dist/, because the CI gate runs `npm test`
before anything is built, and a laptop's dist/ is whatever the last build
left. A second staged build, with both licence files deleted and maps
turned back on, must be refused, so the ticket's acceptance criterion is
itself a test. The first build plants stale maps in dist/ to prove the
clean step works.

Also corrects publish.yml's comment that `files` is ["dist"].

fix(artifact): publish no sourcemaps (rich-artifact-c9k.2) (#132)

* fix(artifact): publish no sourcemaps (rich-artifact-c9k.2)

The tarball carried 200 .map files, every one naming a source under
../../src/, which package.json#files does not publish. Each resolved to a
path absent from a consumer's node_modules, and each .js/.d.ts carried a
sourceMappingURL pointing at it.

dist/ is the npm artifact and nothing else, so the root tsconfig now emits
neither sourceMap nor declarationMap. Excluding *.map through `files`
instead would have left the sourceMappingURL comments dangling, which is
the same dead reference in a different place. Publishing src/ was the
other way to make the maps resolve; it was not taken because tsc's ES2022
output keeps its comments and reads as the source minus its types, so the
maps bought a debugging consumer little for ~1 MB more and a published
src/ layout contract.

tsconfig.demo.json turns sourceMap back on: dist-demo/ sits beside src/
and examples/, so its maps resolve and local debugging keeps them.

npm pack --dry-run: 404 files / 1.8 MB unpacked -> 204 files / 1.1 MB,
zero .map entries.

* fix(build): build dist/ from empty so stale output cannot ship (rich-artifact-c9k.2)

tsc never deletes what it no longer emits, and package.json#files ships
all of dist/. A checkout built before the previous commit kept its .map
files through a rebuild, and a hand-run npm publish would have carried
them into the tarball still naming the unpublished src/. The same held
for the output of any module deleted or renamed since the last clean.

build now runs clean first, so dist/ is exactly what tsc emits from src/
today. Excluding *.map through files was not taken: it would state the
no-maps decision a second time and leave other stale output shipping.
